newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Ramos wants oil companies claims settled.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Ramos wants oil companies claims settled.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Wednesday he has ordered three government departments to complete preparatory work for paying 2.5 billion pesos in claims by the country's local oil refiners from a government fund.

Ramos said at his weekly press conference that he has asked the Department of Finance, the Department of Budget and Management and the Office of the Executive Secretary to "work so we can source the 2.5 billion pesos to pay for the back claims of the oil companies."
The government through the Oil Price Stabilisation Fund (OPSF) owes oil firms Petron Corp, Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp and Caltex (Philippines) Inc a total of 2.5 billion pesos.
The OPSF, now in a deficit, is a buffer fund created to cushion domestic pump prices from drastic fluctuations in crude prices and the foreign exchange rate.
Earlier, the finance department said the claims may be paid from a supplementary budget from Congress.
